title: Inside Tungsten West's £71 Million Restart Financing
subtitle: Government Capital, Project Expenditure and Refinancing Risk at Hemerdon
abstract: The National Wealth Fund's investment changes the financing available for Hemerdon's restart through £36 million of equity and a £25 million core loan, with a further £10 million of uncommitted lending capacity accounting for the £71 million headline. Tungsten West reports a fully funded restart pathway and commissioning progress. Equity absorbs residual project risk without scheduled repayment, while the loan's announced 366-day tenor makes the timing of production, customer collections and refinancing consequential. This assessment reconstructs the instruments and reconciles October's £40–45 million remaining-project-spend guidance with two distinct sensitivities: a £5.75 million incremental cost and rate stress, and the deferral of £15 million of expected receipts in the original August plan. The latter produces approximately £2 million negative cash on published aggregate totals, or £1 million using rounded detail. These scenarios identify expenditure and timing exposures within dated disclosures; neither establishes current liquidity or repayment capacity. The next financial assessment depends on a reconciled cash and debt schedule and evidence that commissioning is converting into dependable collections.

pages.heading: 1  Financing the restart
paragraphs: Tungsten West's £71 million financing headline contains £61 million of gross equity and core-loan funding, alongside a £10 million uncommitted accordion. The National Wealth Fund (NWF) transaction therefore brings both capital that the company reports raising or drawing and an option for further borrowing that requires agreement. Full drawdown of the £25 million core loan was disclosed by accounts approval on 2 September, advancing the financing beyond its August announcement. Management describes Hemerdon's restart as fully funded and reports commissioning progress. [S1, S2, S3]

The composition matters because the £36 million equity contribution absorbs project risk without scheduled repayment, while the core loan places a financing obligation alongside the operating ramp. NWF capital supports redevelopment and the refinancing of earlier short-term debt, but the new loan's announced 366-day tenor gives the company a relatively short period in which to establish dependable cash generation or arrange replacement funding. [S1, S2, S4, S5]

October's £40–45 million remaining-project-spend estimate provides a useful measure of work still to be financed and executed, although operating costs sit outside its scope. Mapping that estimate to the financing instruments directs attention to how expenditure and collections fall within the financing horizon. [S2]

after: The investment case consequently turns on the quality and timing of execution after funding. Processing progress and a commercial offtake agreement strengthen the route to sales; their financial value will emerge as saleable output becomes collected cash. The accepted model quantifies selected cost and receipt sensitivities so that investors and lenders can examine those dependencies without treating a financing announcement as a cash-flow forecast.

pages.heading: 2  Operating progress and cash conversion
paragraphs: Hemerdon's tungsten and tin redevelopment in Devon sits within Drakelands Restoration Limited (DRL), a wholly owned Tungsten West subsidiary. The August facility proposal identifies DRL as borrower with group guarantees, linking project execution to obligations across the corporate structure. That distinction matters when assessing liquidity: the location and restrictions of cash determine whether a group balance can meet a particular project's bills. [S1, S4]

The issuer's September processing announcement and October commissioning update show progress toward generating revenue. Fine-gravity wet commissioning in the third quarter and coarse-gravity wet commissioning in October are reported as achieved milestones. Their significance is the opportunity to demonstrate sustained plant performance, through which ore throughput and recovery translate into payable output. A plant can be commissioning successfully while volumes, unit costs and collection patterns are still developing. [S2, S6]

The eight-year Elmet agreement announced on 23 September provides a commercial outlet for 1,000 tonnes of contained WO3 annually, with variable pricing linked to ammonium paratungstate (APT). It strengthens market access while leaving receipts dependent on deliveries and the contractual price at settlement. With variable pricing, the issuer's nominal value above £1.4 billion at prevailing prices and exchange rates carries no revenue guarantee. The additional 500-tonne processing provision still requires agreement on commercial and delivery terms and reasonable endeavours. [S7]

exhibit.title: Exhibit 2  Evidence required as the restart advances
rows: Sustained hours, throughput, recovery and cost per payable unit.
Product acceptance, delivery schedule, invoice pricing and collection terms.
Production and shipment reconciliation before treating guidance as receipts.
Monthly cash minimum, executed maturity and an agreed source of repayment.

after: Management's FY2028 outlook exceeds 3,300 tonnes of contained WO3 and 600 tonnes of tin. As production builds toward that guidance, recovery and product acceptance will influence the payable volume, while invoice and payment terms determine how quickly sales replenish cash used in the restart. Delays can therefore affect liquidity even where the eventual sales opportunity remains intact. [S2]

For an investor, this makes shipment and collection data the natural successors to commissioning announcements. For a public capital provider, the same observations indicate whether financed capacity is becoming usable supply. The evidence documents this progression without isolating the additional output caused by government intervention.

pages.heading: 3  Capital structure and financing terms
paragraphs: Within the core transaction, equity and debt expose capital providers to different parts of Hemerdon's economics. The £36 million equity contribution participates in residual returns and changes ownership, giving the company capital without a scheduled principal payment. The £25 million loan brings a repayment claim into the restart timetable, while any subsequent use of the £10 million accordion would require commitment and add indebtedness. The announced shareholder arrangements also give NWF specified board nomination or observer, information and veto rights, providing a basis for oversight alongside its financial exposure. [S1, S3, S4]

The disclosed loan pricing makes time consequential. October terms specify SONIA plus an initial margin of 5.5 percentage points, with a further percentage point each quarter. A slower ramp can thus defer receipts while the margin rises. The repayment calendar nevertheless requires the executed agreement: the original announcement measures the 366-day term from definitive agreement, whereas the accounts refer to drawdown, leaving the precise maturity unresolved. [S1, S2, S4]

after: The filed group security agreement provides documentary evidence of fixed and floating security and a negative pledge, naming DRL, Tungsten West, Tungsten West Services and Aggregates West as chargors and GLAS as trustee. Its financed-equipment exclusions make the relationship with other creditors particularly relevant. The deed references a loan agreement without naming the lender, so attribution to NWF remains an inference from its timing and parties. Registration supplies a diligence starting point; facility linkage, priority and collateral value still require the complete financing documents. [S8]

Equipment funding adds a longer-dated source of finance and a separate service burden. October disclosure identifies £11 million current equipment finance and approximately £22 million for ordered machines, with three-to-five-year terms and indicative pricing around 10%. Reconciling their overlap and draw schedule with April's £22.3 million agreement is necessary before assessing aggregate debt or future cash service. [S2, S9]

pages.heading: 4  Remaining expenditure and the cash bridge
paragraphs: October's £40–45 million remaining-project-spend guidance describes the redevelopment work ahead, with £25–35 million falling in FY2027 and the balance in the following financial year. The model's £42.5 million midpoint is an analyst convention within that range. Because financial years end on 31 March and operating costs are excluded, the guidance needs to be mapped to monthly payments and operating cash flows before it can inform a liquidity forecast. [S2]

The audited starting point is £25,485,511 of general-use group cash at 31 March 2026, alongside a separately restricted £14,912,042 restoration escrow. The intervening financing changes what the company can fund, but September publication of those accounts leaves their cash observation at March. The FY2026 net equity proceeds of £41,029,253 and convertible-note cash issuance of £5,205,000 already contribute to that opening stock. A post-March reconstruction must begin with the stock and then follow subsequent movements. [S1]

after: The bridge illustrates why gross funding does not measure construction headroom. The May facility, subsequent bridge repayment and NWF receipts sit among operating expenditure, capital payments and other financing movements whose exact dates and amounts are needed to close the cash rollforward. Comparing the £61 million transaction with October remaining spend would omit these uses and the receipts arising during the same period. [S1, S2, S5, S10]

Accounting presentation introduces a further reconciliation issue. The March £10.642 million deposits balance mainly reflects rebuild purchase orders, so cash committed to redevelopment extends beyond the PPE acquisition line. Meanwhile, the £197.212 million convertible-note conversion and £167.324 million fair-value remeasurement moved no cash. A bank-reconciled ledger and unpaid capex schedule would resolve these distinctions and allow management's fully funded pathway to be examined as dated financial headroom. The available record supports no finding of a current shortage. [S1]

pages.heading: 5  Cost exposure and dependence on receipts
paragraphs: The October spending range makes the scale of incremental cost exposure visible. Moving from the £42.5 million midpoint to £45 million adds £2.5 million, to which the model adds the company's approximately £3 million sensitivity for a three-month delay involving fallback processing. A separate analyst rate proxy, one percentage point on a constant £25 million for one year, contributes £0.25 million. Together they produce a £5.75 million increment above the midpoint reference. [S1, S2]

This combination is useful because execution pressure can affect both expenditure and financing cost. It remains a deliberately bounded stress: the rate proxy isolates exposure without reconstructing SONIA, quarterly margin steps or fees, and the delay cost has no fiscal-year assignment. No accordion draw is assumed. The result therefore measures a selected increase in uses, leaving the amount and timing of any financing response to a fuller cash forecast.

−2 ending cash. £15m below the original reserve target.

after: The original August funding plan exposes a separate dependence on collections. Its £61 million equity and core loan sat alongside £7 million opening cash, £5 million provision recovery and £15 million anticipated receipts. Published aggregate sources and uses both totalled £88 million, including a £13 million reserve. Deferring the receipts while holding the other plan items fixed leaves approximately £2 million negative cash on those totals, a £15 million shortfall against the reserve target. [S4]

The separately rounded use lines total £87 million, producing approximately £1 million negative cash under the same counterfactual. Retaining that rounding difference avoids false precision while preserving the economic finding: the original reserve depended materially on the timing of operating receipts. The exercise concerns the August plan at an unspecified peak funding date and makes no claim that the receipts failed to arrive. Its scope overlaps subsequent expenditure guidance, so combining it with the October £5.75 million stress would misstate a current financing requirement.

pages.heading: 6  Cash generation within the loan horizon
paragraphs: The loan's announced 366-day tenor places repayment or refinancing close to the period in which Hemerdon is establishing its operating cash cycle. October's FY2028 guidance includes approximately £26 million NWF principal and interest and £6 million equipment service, alongside £70–75 million cash operating costs and sustaining capex. The separate £7 million Hargreaves payment takes the model's selected annual cash reference to £109–114 million, with a £111.5 million midpoint. These amounts show why production economics and the financing calendar need to be assessed together. [S2]

The model relates that selected cash reference to tungsten receipts using 3,300 tonnes of contained WO3, 100 mtu per tonne, 79.5% payability and a modeled 3% deduction. At those coefficients, each £1 per mtu of GBP APT reference generates £254,479.50 in the annual receipt proxy, giving £438.15 per mtu at the midpoint cash requirement. This calculation isolates the sensitivity to price and payable volume without supplying a forward commodity forecast or substituting for Elmet's executed pricing terms. [S2]

exhibit.title: Exhibit 6  FY2028 tungsten-only core coverage reference

after: The coverage reference omits tin and aggregate receipts as well as remaining restart capex, growth expenditure, cash taxes and working capital. Because the omitted flows run in both directions, the result supplies neither full project break-even nor a conservative bound. Its value is diagnostic: it shows how a defined set of cash uses compares with a defined tungsten revenue coefficient, while keeping the missing parts of the project cash flow visible.

At fixed coefficients, a £100 per mtu reference-price change moves the annual tungsten receipt proxy by about £25.45 million. Achieved output and collection timing determine how much of that price exposure becomes cash available for creditors. A strong price can improve refinancing prospects, but a slower ramp may still absorb working capital and defer collections as financing costs rise.

Refinancing would move the repayment obligation to a later date and on terms still to be agreed. The relevant test is therefore the alignment of dependable collections with contractual payments, together with the availability and economics of replacement capital. A monthly forecast through the executed maturity, supported by the equipment-debt schedule, is necessary to assess repayment capacity and covenant headroom.

pages.heading: 7  Implications for institutional capital
paragraphs: For equity investors, NWF's investment reduces dependence on uncertain access to restart funding and gives the company a stronger basis for pursuing its commissioning programme. The return on that capital will depend on the cash remaining after operating costs, investment and financing obligations. Monitoring payable output and collections therefore provides more information about the developing investment case than the financing headline alone; any further capital raise would also need to be assessed for its ownership and dilution consequences.

A lender's analysis begins with the same operating evidence but asks when cash becomes available against a specific repayment calendar. The definitive facility must settle the tenor origin, rate conventions and quarterly step dates, as well as covenants, cure rights and accordion conditions. Security diligence must then reconcile the group deed with financed-equipment exclusions and creditor priority. Together, these documents determine how much flexibility exists if the commercial ramp takes longer than expected.

Public capital providers have an additional implementation test. The equity investment carries residual exposure, the loan requires recovery, and the industrial objective depends on commissioned capacity becoming dependable supply. Monitoring those objectives separately allows strategic progress to be recognized without assuming it proves a financial return. Government procurement remains subject to a subsequent agreement, with no agreed price floor disclosed. [S3, S4]

exhibit.title: Exhibit 7  Evidence that would change the financial assessment
rows: Remaining obligations funded with clear headroom, or rising unpaid commitments and restricted cash.
Sustained conversion toward guidance, or repeated commissioning and acceptance delays.
Contracted output converts to cash, or working capital absorbs financing.
Agreed replacement capital or cash cover, or an unresolved maturity approaching.
No double-counted capacity and manageable cash service, or concentrated payment pressure.

after: Hemerdon has progressed to disclosed equity funding and loan drawdown, with processing milestones and a binding commercial agreement supporting management's restart pathway. The next financial judgement will be better informed by how much saleable material is delivered, how promptly customers pay and how the repayment timetable is funded. The instrument reconstruction and scenario results identify where those observations matter most, while a reconciled liquidity and debt schedule remains the prerequisite for underwriting current headroom or investment value.

pages.heading: 8  Methodology and primary source guide
paragraphs: This memorandum uses the evidence register and model accepted in Phase 1B at commit 772f2f4c02631f533a0a893849c9bedb8a6ff8ad, with a research cutoff of 4 November 2026. The editorial revision retains the original amounts, reporting dates and company/project scope. Financial years end on 31 March. Audited balances, issuer guidance, filed terms and analyst scenarios are identified according to their evidentiary role.

All four principal findings reconcile to the accepted workbook. Independent LibreOffice validation tested 32 cases with zero remaining failures and no differences across 167 cached formulas; the earlier missing-input failures and their corrections remain preserved in the audit trail. The publication workbook is byte-identical to that accepted version. Native Microsoft Excel execution remains unverified.

The evidence appendix and model guide contain claim-level locators, scenario assumptions and metric definitions. Current cash, aggregate current debt, a complete funding gap, valuation/NPV/IRR, DSCR, covenant headroom, repayment sufficiency and default probability remain outside the supported conclusions. The analysis also makes no causal estimate of additional production attributable to public financing.
after: Prepared for final publication review. Independent human financial/editorial approval and source-specific rights clearance remain release conditions. No original AMC tables, source PDFs or proprietary benchmark series are reproduced, and the publication expresses no investment recommendation.
